title: Rav Kahana bar Tachlifa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Eruvin 8b: “Rav Kahana bar Tachlifa said in the name of Rav Kahana bar Minyomi, in the name of Rav Kahana, Rav’s teacher — and some say Rav Kahana mar Malkiyu [supplied מר; the named Talmud witness has בר], that is Rav Kahana, Rav’s teacher … Rav Kahana said: Since this is a teaching of Kahanas, I will say something about it.” The Bach reads (instead of “in the name of Rav Kahana, Rav’s teacher”) “in the name of Rav Kahana Rabbah, and some say Rav Kahana bar Malkiyu, that is Rav Kahana Rabbah.” Dikdukei Soferim reads “Rav Huna bar Tachlifa in the name of Rav Kahana Rabbah.” In the Pesaro, Venice רפה, Giustiniani, Basel and Constantinople printings, it reads (instead of bar Minyomi) bar Mattityah, and so it is in the Or Zarua, siman 114, and in Yuchasin.

He is likewise mentioned in Menachot (supplied סי:; the exchange is at 66b): “Rav Kahana bar Tachlifa raised an objection to Rav Kahana bar Mattityah.” In Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, beginning of halakhah 9: “Rabbi Zeira, Kahana bar Tachlifa, Chanan bar Ba in the name of Rav.”

notes.text: Saved Davidson Eruvin8b has bar Malkiyu where the supplied first citation has mar. The Kahanas are the named transmitters in an alley-beam discussion, not priests discussing priestly law. The date רפה is kept literally without an assumed millennium; Giustiniani remains a separate printing. The supplied סי: locator is preserved alongside matching Davidson Menachot66b, replacing the unsupported60b resolution; no printed correction history is claimed.
